Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

July bookings are expected to be higher than in June because the Vale Road clinic is moving its Tuesday appointments to the hub for four weeks. Coordinator Mara Venn said, “We can plan around the dates; we cannot guess the passenger count and call it confirmed.” The current working rota is a shared spreadsheet, and the printed copy at the hub desk is updated on Fridays.

There are eleven active volunteer drivers. Four can take wheelchair users in the hub’s lift-equipped minivan, while the other seven drive their own cars and can take passengers who can step into a standard vehicle. Drivers enter their usual availability by the twentieth of each month. Some have also offered one-off dates by text, but those dates are not in the spreadsheet until a coordinator checks them. The July sheet currently has six such text offers waiting to be checked. Last month, a date was entered against the wrong driver after two messages arrived close together, so coordinator Ben Iles has asked staff to match each offer to its sender before adding it.

The hub minivan is booked for routine servicing on July 8. The garage expects to return it by the end of that day, but has not guaranteed the time. If the minivan is not back before the July 9 morning pickups, those rides need to be checked with the passengers and reassigned to a suitable vehicle or rescheduled; the team must not mark them as covered just because a driver is listed. The service booking does not affect the other cars. The minivan’s wheelchair ramp was inspected in June and passed. A spare tie-down strap is kept in the locked equipment cabinet, and the cabinet key is held by the desk lead.

Most recurring journeys are short trips to the clinic, pharmacy, or grocery cooperative. The Tuesday clinic run from North Quay usually needs the minivan because two regular passengers use wheelchairs. One passenger, Elsie Marr, has asked for a pickup between 8:30 and 8:45 rather than the earlier window used in May. Her message says, “The new appointment time is later, so please don’t send a car before half past eight.” The clinic has not said whether the change applies to the other Tuesday passengers. On Thursdays, the grocery cooperative accepts arrivals only from 10:00 to 11:30, and volunteers usually wait at the side entrance rather than the loading bay.

Trip requests are collected on paper at the desk and by phone. The desk log has three July requests that are not yet assigned: a pharmacy pickup for Mr. Lorne in Bellmarsh on July 4, a clinic return for Peta Simm on July 16, and a grocery trip for two residents of Linton Fold on July 23. The log gives contact numbers for all three, but the July 23 entry does not say whether either resident needs a wheelchair-accessible vehicle. The caller is listed as “N. D.”, and no full name appears elsewhere in the log. Desk volunteer Asha Pell said, “I can call back, but I don’t want to assume which household it was.”

The rota includes a column for the assigned driver, pickup window, vehicle type, passenger confirmation, and backup plan. Passenger confirmation means the passenger or their listed contact has agreed to the pickup details; it is not enough that a message was left. A blank backup-plan cell means no backup has been recorded, not that the trip has no risk. Coordinators normally review unconfirmed trips on the Monday before the travel week. The June review found that two passengers had not received a revised pickup time after a driver swap, so the team wants the July review to make changes visible before printed sheets are handed out.

1. Items already recorded for July: the July 2 North Quay clinic run is assigned to driver Oren Pike in the minivan, with both wheelchair passengers marked confirmed. The July 9 run is also listed in the minivan, assigned to Oren, but its backup-plan cell is blank and passenger confirmation is marked “pending.” The July 16 North Quay run is assigned to driver Salma Reed in her own car, although the passenger notes field says “two chairs”; no one has checked whether this is a data-entry error or a change in passenger needs. The July 23 clinic run has no driver entered. These entries are in the current spreadsheet, not additional bookings supplied by the clinic.

Volunteer availability has a few specific limits. Oren Pike is unavailable July 15 through July 19. Salma Reed can drive only within the town centre on weekdays and has not offered to take a wheelchair passenger. Jo March is willing to drive to Bellmarsh but cannot take evening pickups. Tavi Noor has said they may be available on July 23, depending on a work shift, and asked for confirmation by July 18. No one has yet confirmed whether Tavi’s shift will allow the trip. Driver Kit Rowan has asked to be removed from the printed emergency-contact list because their phone number changed; the hub has the new number, but the updated contact card is not yet printed.

The hub tries to pair drivers and passengers consistently where possible, but continuity is not guaranteed when a driver is unavailable. A passenger may decline a proposed replacement, and the rota should not show a ride as accepted until the passenger or listed contact agrees. If a trip cannot be covered by an appropriate vehicle and an agreed driver, coordinators contact the passenger to discuss rescheduling; the notes do not authorize staff to cancel a trip without that conversation. The team has no budget for taxis in the July plan. Coordinator Mara Venn added, “A gap on the sheet is a prompt to check, not permission to improvise a promise.”

For printing, the hub needs one desk copy and one copy for each driver who is assigned at least one trip. The desk copy should show pending confirmations and blank backup cells clearly. Driver copies should contain only the trips assigned to that driver, plus the hub desk phone number; the desk phone number is already printed on the standard template. The team has not decided whether to include passenger phone numbers on driver copies, and the current template hides them. Any proposed change to that template needs to be raised with Mara before printing rather than assumed.
